services/cli:
`miosa service` operates Services.
`miosa services` and `miosa svc` are aliases.
A named background process inside a sandbox is `miosa daemon`, a different product.

`<project>` is a project name, slug or id.
`<service>` is a service name, slug or id; the CLI resolves the name to the id the API needs.
`<release>` is a release number or id.
Every command accepts `--json`.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `service create <project> <name>` | Create a web service, worker, private service, static site, cron job or database service |
| `service list <project>` | List the project's services |
| `service get <project> <service>` | Show one service |
| `service update <project> <service>` | Change the name, start command, replicas or region |
| `service deploy <project> <service>` | Build and release |
| `service logs <project> <service>` | Show a release's transitions and failure reason |
| `service scale <project> <service>` | Change replicas, region or limits |
| `service start <project> <service>` | Start a stopped service |
| `service stop <project> <service>` | Stop every active release now |
| `service restart <project> <service>` | Queue a release that restarts the service |
| `service delete <project> <service>` | Delete a service and stop its replicas; a database service also deletes its database |
| `service releases <project> <service>` | List releases, newest first |
| `service release <project> <service> <release>` | Show one release |
| `service rollback <project> <service> <release>` | Serve an earlier release again |
| `service promote <project> <service> <release>` | The same as rollback |
| `service cancel <project> <service> <release>` | Cancel a queued or building release |
| `service domains <project> <service>` | Show the private and public addresses |
| `service domains enable <project> <service>` | Give the service a public address |
| `service domains disable <project> <service>` | Remove the public address |
| `service vars list <project> <service>` | List variables, masked |
| `service vars set <project> <service> KEY=VALUE...` | Set variables |
| `service vars unset <project> <service> NAME[,NAME]` | Delete variables |
| `service vars effective <project> <service>` | Show what a deploy would receive |
| `service vars reveal <project> <service> NAME` | Print one value |
| `service runs <project> <service>` | A cron service's recent runs |
| `service connection <project> <service>` | A database service's URLs |
| `service settings <project>` | What each setting does today |
| `service templates` | List the template catalog |
| `service templates apply <project> <slug>` | Apply a template |
| `project vars list <project>` | Shared variables, masked |
| `project vars set <project> KEY=VALUE...` | Set shared variables |
| `project vars unset <project> NAME` | Delete a shared variable |
| `project target list <project>` | List Deploy targets |
| `project target create <project> <name>` | Create a Deploy target |
| `project target duplicate <project> <target> --name <new>` | Copy a Deploy target's services and variables |
| `project target rm <project> <target>` | Delete a Deploy target |

## `service create` flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--type` | `web`, `worker`, `private`, `static`, `schedule` or `database` (default `web`) |
| `--repo`, `--branch`, `--root-dir` | A git source |
| `--image`, `--port` | A container image source |
| `--dockerfile` | Dockerfile path for a git source (needs Services build cells) |
| `--start-command` | Command the service starts with |
| `--replicas` | 1 to 50 |
| `--region` | `us-west`, `us-east` or `us-mia` |
| `--schedule` | Five-field schedule expression, required for `--type schedule` |
| `--env KEY=VALUE` | A variable; repeatable, and a value may be a `${{...}}` reference |
| `--no-public` | Do not give a web or static service a public address |
| `--slug` | Host label (default: from the name) |
| `--deploy-target` | Deploy target name or id (default: the project's default) |

A web or static service gets its public address enabled right after creation unless `--no-public` is passed.
If the address cannot be enabled the service is still created and the CLI prints a warning.

## `service deploy` flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dir` | Upload this local directory as the source |
| `--repo`, `--branch`, `--root-dir` | Deploy a git source |
| `--image`, `--port` | Deploy a container image |
| `--message` | Release message |
| `--wait`, `--timeout` | Follow the release until it is live or fails |
| `--deploy-target` | Deploy target name or id |

With no source flag the service's own source is rebuilt.

## `service get`

`service get` prints the service, including `Pending changes` when a variable write made the running release stale.
The value is `rebuild` (a build-visible variable changed) or `redeploy` (any other variable), and `miosa service deploy` is the action that clears it.

## `service logs`

`logs` prints the newest release's state transitions and its failure reason.
Pass `--release <number|id>` for an older one.
`--follow` is refused until the Services log stream ships; the release events carry the reason a release failed.

## Deploy targets

Every project has a default Deploy target, and the first read creates `production`.
Services, variables and releases live inside one Deploy target; `--deploy-target` picks it and defaults to the project's default.

```bash
miosa project target list shop
miosa project target duplicate shop production --name staging
miosa service list shop --deploy-target staging
```

A duplicate copies services and variables; secrets are generated again and no data or managed database is copied.

## Confirmation

`stop`, `delete`, `rollback` and `promote` ask for confirmation on a terminal and refuse in a script unless `--yes` is passed.

### Deleting a database service

Deleting a database service also deletes its database and every row in it.
It cannot be undone, so it needs the service's exact name, not `--yes`:

- On a terminal, the CLI asks you to type the name.
- In a script, pass `--confirm <exact name>`.
- `--yes` alone is not enough.
- A run with no terminal and no `--confirm` exits with code 2 and sends nothing.
- A `--confirm` that does not match the name exactly also exits with code 2.

```bash
miosa service delete shop Postgres --confirm Postgres
```

`--confirm` needs CLI 2.13.3 or later.

## Automation

Every command is non-interactive with `--yes` (deleting a database service needs `--confirm <name>` instead), prints JSON with `--json`, and exits non-zero on an API error.
The API's error code is preserved; for example a stale settings write exits non-zero with `STALE_SERVICE`.
services/config-file:
A service can carry its settings in a file at the repository root. The same file
works for Docker Host and for Services:

- `miosa.app.yml`, `miosa.app.yaml` or `miosa.app.json`, and
- `miosa.json`.

`railway.json` is read as a compatible fallback, so a project imported from
Railway needs no edit first.

## Rules

**Only the fields the file names change.** A file with one key leaves every other
setting as the project has it. A file is an addition, not a replacement.

**The API still validates.** The merged settings go through the same validation
as a console save, so a file cannot write a value the API would refuse.

**The file wins over the console for the fields it names.** The console shows
which fields came from the file.

## Fields

| File key | Setting | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| `deploy.start` / `startCommand` / `start_command` | Start command | all |
| `deploy.preDeploy` / `preDeployCommand` | Pre-deploy command | all |
| `deploy.healthcheckPath` / `healthcheck_path` | Health check path | web services |
| `deploy.healthcheckTimeout` | Health check timeout, seconds | web services |
| `deploy.restartPolicy` / `restartPolicyType` | `always`, `on_failure` or `never` | all |
| `deploy.maxRetries` / `restartPolicyMaxRetries` | Retries before giving up | all |
| `deploy.replicas` / `numReplicas` | Replicas | all |
| `deploy.cron` / `cronSchedule` | Five-field schedule | cron services |
| `deploy.region` | `us-east`, `us-west` or `us-mia` | all |
| `deploy.sleep` / `sleepApplication` | Sleep when idle, five minutes by default | web services with a public address |
| `build_command` | Build command, Railpack builds only | static services |
| `output_dir` | Directory to serve, relative to the app | static services |

`variables` are read as names; values are not taken from the file.

## What the file cannot carry

Keys with no equivalent are reported in the plan and in the console rather than
dropped quietly: `build.builder`, `build.dockerfilePath`, and anything unknown.

> **Note: Where the value came from**
>
> Every field the file sets is recorded against the file and key that set it, so
> "why is the start command this?" has an answer months later.
services/dedicated-vcpu:
A dedicated size gives a service vCPUs it owns outright.
Each dedicated vCPU is one hardware thread of the host, pinned to your service and never shared with another workload.
Use it when you need steady CPU with no noisy neighbors.

Dedicated sizes are available on Business and above.

## Sizes and prices

Memory is 4 GiB per vCPU.

| Size | vCPU | Memory | Price per month |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dedicated-2` | 2 | 8 GiB | $153.37 |
| `dedicated-4` | 4 | 16 GiB | $306.74 |
| `dedicated-8` | 8 | 32 GiB | $613.48 |
| `dedicated-16` | 16 | 64 GiB | $1,226.95 |

- A dedicated vCPU costs $32.8725 a month ($0.04503 an hour), and memory costs the normal $10.953 per GiB-month.
- A dedicated service is billed for its full size for every second a replica runs, whether the CPU is busy or idle.
- A stopped or sleeping service is not billed for compute.
- The same vCPUs and memory on a shared size cost about 17 percent less, without the guarantee.

## Select a size

Set `shape` in the service settings.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/projects/{id}/services/{sid} \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"settings": {"shape": "dedicated-4"}}'
```

- The size applies to the next deployment.
- `replicas` multiplies it: three replicas of `dedicated-4` use 12 dedicated vCPUs.
- If you also set `limits`, they must fit inside the size.
- Check `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/services/setting-capabilities`: the `shape` entry reads `enforced` when dedicated sizes are available to place.

## Capacity

Dedicated vCPUs come from a fixed pool of 16 threads on each host that carries one.
A deployment is placed only on such a host, and it is refused with `no_capacity` when that host's pool has too few free threads.
A deployment of 16 vCPUs takes a whole host pool.
Free threads return to the pool when a replica stops.
services/domains:
Services reach managed databases through their connection variables.
A web service or a static site can also have a public address.

## Private networking

Private networking between services is not available yet.
One service cannot reach another by a private name, and `private_network` reads `{"enabled": false}`.
The older `private_domain` field (`<service-slug>.miosa.internal`) and the `MIOSA_PRIVATE_DOMAIN` variable do not resolve; do not build on them.

Managed databases connect automatically from any host.
Reference a database's connection in the service's Variables:

```text
DATABASE_URL=${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}
REDIS_URL=${{Redis.REDIS_URL}}
```

To call another service of the project, give it a public address and call that.
The service's Networking tab in the console shows the same.

## Public address

```bash
miosa service domains shop API
miosa service domains enable shop API --label api
miosa service domains disable shop API
```

`enable` gives the service:

```text
https://<label>.<your-org>.miosa.app
```

The label defaults to the service's slug and must be lowercase a-z, 0-9 and `-`.
The label is unique across your organization.
TLS is issued and renewed by the platform; there is no certificate to install.

`disable` removes the public address and leaves the private one in place.
The service keeps running; it just stops being reachable from the internet.

## What serves a public address

The public address routes to the healthy replicas of the service's active release.
A release that is not `active` does not receive traffic.

If the service has idle sleep enabled, a request to a sleeping service wakes it and waits for it.
A service without a public address has no request signal, so it never sleeps.

## Reading the address in code

TypeScript:

```typescript
const service = await miosa.services.get(serviceId);
console.log(service.private_network);       // { enabled: false } while private networking is not available
console.log(service.public_address.url);    // null until enabled
```

Python:

```python
service = miosa.services.get(service_id)
print(service["private_network"])
print(service["public_address"]["url"])
```

## Custom domains

The public address is on `miosa.app`.
A custom domain on your own DNS zone is a separate product: register it, add the CNAME it shows and let MIOSA verify it.
That flow lives under Domains, not under a service, so one domain can outlive a service.

## When ingress is off

If public addresses are not switched on for the platform, `enable` answers `INGRESS_DISABLED` (404).
The service still runs, but has no address to reach it on, and `miosa service settings shop` reports `public_address` as `unsupported`.
services/environments:
An environment is a copy of a project that runs on its own.
Every project starts with a `production` environment.
Add `staging`, a preview, or anything else you need.

Each environment has its own services, variables and releases.
A change in staging does not touch production.

## Switch and fork on the canvas

The environment name sits in the canvas top bar, next to the project name.
Open it to see every environment of the project and to switch between them.
The canvas reloads for the environment you pick, and the address carries it as `?env=<name>`.

Choose **Fork** to create a new environment from the one you are looking at.
Give it a name.
MIOSA copies the services and variables, then shows a summary of what was copied and what was skipped.

## From the API

```text
GET  /api/v1/projects/:id/environments
POST /api/v1/projects/:id/environments/:env/duplicate   {"name": "staging"}
```

`duplicate` returns the new environment, the services and variables it copied, and the entries it skipped.
The project's service routes accept `?env=<name>`; without it they use `production`.

## Where to go next

- [Variables](/docs/services/variables): variables and references are per environment.
- [Releases and rollback](/docs/services/releases): each environment has its own releases.
- Docker Host has its own [environments](/docs/docker-host/environments) for the former Docker Host deployments.
services/logs:
The service panel has a **Logs** tab with three views.

| View | Shows |
|---|---|
| Runtime | The newest lines each replica printed, with the replica's state. |
| Build | The log of the build that produced a release, with whether it finished. |
| Events | The state transitions of a release and the reason when it failed. |

A service that runs a container image has no build, so its Build view is empty.

## Runtime logs

Runtime logs are per replica.
Each replica reports its state and its lines, or an error when its log could not be read.
Each replica is listed separately, and the `replica` parameter reads one.

```text
GET /api/v1/projects/:id/services/:sid/logs?tail=200&replica=<id>
```

## Build logs

```text
GET /api/v1/projects/:id/services/:sid/builds/latest/logs?tail=200
GET /api/v1/projects/:id/services/:sid/builds/:build_id/logs?after=<offset>
```

The response carries the text, the offset to continue from, and `complete` once the build has finished.
Ask again with `after` set to the last offset to follow a running build.

## Events and failure reasons

```bash
miosa service logs shop API
```

The CLI prints the newest release's state transitions and its failure reason.
It does not stream runtime output.

## Where to go next

- [Releases and rollback](/docs/services/releases): the release states the events describe.
- [Replicas and scaling](/docs/services/replicas): what a replica is.
services/metrics:
Every service reports its own request series: requests, errors, error rate, and
response latency at p50 and p95.

```bash
miosa service metrics lumen API
miosa service metrics lumen API --range 24h --json
```

The same series is at `GET /api/v1/projects/:id/services/:sid/metrics/series?range=`
with `15m`, `1h`, `6h`, `24h` or `7d`, scope `projects:read`.

## Reading it honestly

The server buckets the series and reports `step_seconds`: 60 for `15m` and `1h`,
300 for `6h`, 900 for `24h`, and 3600 for `7d`. The full timeline comes back even
in a quiet window, with null fields where nothing happened; a point is empty when
`requests` is null, and the CLI prints a dash rather than a zero.

`available` names what is actually measured. For a service that is `requests` and
`latency`; **cpu, memory and network are not collected for services**, and the CLI
says so under the table instead of printing empty columns.

> **Note: Web vitals**
>
> Real-user web vitals (LCP, INP, FCP, TTFB, CLS) are collected for static and web
> services that include the beacon, and come back under `web_vitals` with
> `available.web_vitals`. They are reported separately because they measure the
> browser, not the server.
services/middleware:
Edge middleware runs in front of a server service, before the request reaches
your process: redirects, rewrites, header changes, and optionally a published
function that can answer, continue or rewrite the request.

It is a structured rule set, so it is written as a file rather than a pile of
flags:

```bash
miosa middleware shop API --from middleware.json
miosa middleware shop API           # what is configured now
miosa middleware shop API --off     # remove the rules and the function
```

```json
{
  "rules": [
    { "path": "/old/*", "redirect": { "to": "/new", "status": 308 } },
    { "path": "/api/*", "request_headers": { "set": { "x-plan": "pro" } } }
  ],
  "function": { "slug": "gate", "paths": ["/app/*"], "timeout_ms": 250, "on_error": "closed" }
}
```

Rules run in order and there can be up to fifty of them. A `path` is either an
exact path or a prefix ending in `/*`, where `$1` is the rest of the path. Each
rule carries exactly one of a `redirect` (with an optional `301`, `302`, `303`,
`307` or `308`, default `307`), a `rewrite`, and/or header changes.

The function answers `x-miosa-middleware: next` to let the request continue, and
may add `x-miosa-middleware-request-<name>` or `x-miosa-middleware-rewrite`. Any
other answer is returned to the client. With `on_error: "closed"`, a failing
function answers `503 edge_middleware_unavailable`; with `open`, the request
continues.

Protected header names are refused, including `host`, `content-length`,
`transfer-encoding`, `connection`, `upgrade`, `x-internal-*`, `x-miosa-*` and
`x-forwarded-*`.

> **Note: It applies in seconds**
>
> A change applies within about five seconds at every edge node. Validation errors
> name the field (`settings.edge_middleware.<path>`), so a typo in a rule is easy to
> find.
services/overview:
Services are the apps a project runs.
A service is one of four common types, plus cron jobs and database services:

| Type | What it is |
|---|---|
| Web service | A process that serves HTTP on a public address. |
| Worker | A process with no port and no address. It runs until it stops. |
| Private service | A process with no public address. Private networking between services is not available yet, so nothing else reaches it by name; it can reach managed databases through their connection variables. |
| Static site | Pre-built files served from the edge. |
| Cron job | A command on a five-field cron schedule, with run history and output. |
| Database service | A managed Postgres or Redis bound to the project. |

Every service belongs to a project and an environment.
A project starts with a `production` environment; add `staging` or anything else you need.

## What a service has

- **Releases.** Every deploy is an immutable release with a number, a state and a reason when it fails.
- **Variables.** Sealed at rest, masked on read, and able to reference another service, a shared variable or a generated secret.
- **An address.** Every service is assigned a private name. A web service or static site can also have a public address.
- **Settings.** Replicas, region, start command, health check, restart policy, volumes and idle sleep.

## The lifecycle

1. Create the service with a source: a git repository, a container image or an uploaded archive.
2. Deploy it. MIOSA builds it and starts a release.
3. The release becomes `active` when its replicas pass their health checks.
4. Deploy again to change it, or roll back to an earlier release. Rollback serves the earlier built image, so nothing is rebuilt.

## Where to go next

- [Quick start](/docs/services/quickstart): a repository to a live URL, then Postgres, a worker, a domain and a rollback.
- [Services and types](/docs/services/services): the source, settings and address of each type.
- [Variables](/docs/services/variables): references between services and generated secrets.
- [Releases](/docs/services/releases): deploy, promote, roll back and cancel.
- [CLI](/docs/services/cli) and [SDKs](/docs/services/sdk): the same operations from a terminal or code.

## Migrating from Railway

The model maps directly:

| Railway | MIOSA |
|---|---|
| Project | Project |
| Service | Service (web service, worker, private service or static site) |
| Environment | Environment |
| Deployment | Release |
| Variables and shared variables | Variables and shared variables |
| Custom domain | Public address |

`miosa service` operates Services.
Services use `/projects/:id/services` and `/services/:id`; the separate Deploy product keeps its own `/deployments` routes.
services/previews:
A preview environment is a copy of your project's default environment that runs a pull request.
Open a pull request and MIOSA creates the environment, deploys the pull request's branch, and comments the addresses on the pull request.
Close or merge it and the environment is deleted.

## What happens

| Pull request event | What MIOSA does |
|---|---|
| Opened or reopened | Forks the default environment as `pr-<number>`, deploys every service from the pull request's branch, and comments the addresses |
| New commit pushed | Redeploys the services of `pr-<number>` |
| Closed or merged | Deletes `pr-<number>` and nothing else |

Each server service in the preview is named `<service>-pr-<number>`.
Variables are copied from the environment it was forked from.
A preview never changes the environment it came from.

## Turn it on

Open the project's **Settings** in the console and choose **Previews**.
Set the repository as `owner/name`, switch previews on, and save.
The page shows the webhook URL and the secret to paste into GitHub.

In the GitHub repository, add a webhook:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Payload URL | The URL shown in Previews, `https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/hooks/git/<project id>` |
| Content type | `application/json` |
| Secret | The secret from Previews |
| Events | Pull requests only |

The repository you set must match GitHub's `full_name` exactly, or deliveries are ignored.
A delivery is accepted only when its signature matches the secret.
The secret is write-only: it is never shown again, so keep a copy or set a new one.

## Cost control

| Setting | Default | Range |
|---|---|---|
| `max_open` | 3 | 1 to 20 |
| `ttl_hours` | 72 | 1 to 720 |

A fourth preview is refused while three are open.
A preview for a pull request nobody closed is deleted after 72 hours.
Raise or lower both in Previews.

## From the API

```text
GET    /api/v1/projects/:id/previews
PUT    /api/v1/projects/:id/previews
DELETE /api/v1/projects/:id/previews/:preview_id
```

`PUT` replaces the row, so send the whole object: `{repository, enabled, max_open, ttl_hours, secret}`.
A blank or absent `secret` keeps the one already stored.
The row you get back reports `has_secret`, never the secret, and the `webhook_path` to use.
These routes need the `projects:read` and `projects:write` scopes.

## Where to go next

- [Environments](/docs/services/environments): fork an environment by hand.
- [Variables](/docs/services/variables): what a preview copies.
services/protection:
Protection and the WAF are enforced at the edge, in front of the service, so they
apply before a request reaches your process.

## Password and share links

```bash
miosa protection shop API                            # is it protected?
miosa protection shop API --password 'open-sesame'
miosa protection shop API --share-link --expires 3600
miosa protection shop API --revoke <link-id>
miosa protection shop API --off
```

The password is never shown again. A share link is a way past it for one person:
the `msl_...` token is shown once, and expires after `--expires` seconds (seven
days by default, at most ninety). A visitor uses it as `?miosa_share=<token>` or
with an `x-miosa-share-token` header.

Protection can also be set on a Deploy target or on an environment kind, and the
rows resolve service over environment over kind. That is why a preview environment
can be protected without touching each service in it.

## WAF

```bash
miosa waf shop API
miosa waf shop API --mode enforce --deny 203.0.113.0/24 --rate 120
miosa waf shop API --allow 198.51.100.0/24
miosa waf shop API --attack-mode on
miosa waf shop API --off
```

- `--mode` is `off`, `observe` or `enforce`.
- `--allow`/`--deny` take IPs or CIDRs (`ip_allow`/`ip_deny` on the wire).
- `--rate` is requests per minute per source; `0` clears the limit.
- `--attack-mode` serves a JavaScript challenge to browsers and `403` to
  everything else.

**Country rules read only the trusted `x-miosa-country` header that the edge
sets.** There is no GeoIP lookup of our own: if a request arrives without that
header the country rules are skipped, and the WAF document says whether they can
act at all with `country_rules_active`.

> **Note: Observe before enforce**
>
> Run `--mode observe` for a day first. The WAF reports what it would have blocked,
> so you can see a wrong CIDR before it turns into a page full of 403s.
services/quickstart:
This walkthrough takes a repository to a live URL, then adds a database, a worker and a domain.
Every step has a CLI form and an SDK form.

## Before you start

- A MIOSA account with an API key (`msk_...`) or a signed-in CLI.
- A project. `miosa project create shop --workspace-id <workspace>` creates one; `miosa project list` shows the others.
- A repository MIOSA can clone, or a container image.

Export the key once:

```bash
export MIOSA_API_KEY=msk_your_key
```

## 1. Create a web service

```bash
miosa service create shop API --type web \
  --repo https://github.com/acme/api \
  --branch main \
  --start-command "node server.js" \
  --replicas 2 \
  --env NODE_ENV=production
```

`--type web` stores the API's `server` kind, which can have a public address.
`--type private` stores the same kind but never gets one.
The command prints the service, its private address and, once enabled, its public address.

TypeScript:

```typescript
const service = await miosa.services.create(projectId, {
  name: "API",
  type: "web",
  source: { type: "git", ref: "https://github.com/acme/api", branch: "main" },
  settings: { start_command: "node server.js", replicas: 2 },
});
const address = await miosa.services.enablePublicAddress(service.id);
console.log(address.url); // https://api.acme.miosa.app
```

Python:

```python
service = miosa.services.create(
    project_id,
    "API",
    type="web",
    source={"type": "git", "ref": "https://github.com/acme/api", "branch": "main"},
    settings={"start_command": "node server.js", "replicas": 2},
)
address = miosa.services.enable_public_address(service["id"])
print(address["url"])
```

## 2. Deploy it

```bash
miosa service deploy shop API --message "first deploy" --wait
```

`--wait` polls the release until it is live or fails.
Without it you get the queued release and can check it with `miosa service releases shop API`.

```typescript
const release = await miosa.services.deploy(service.id, { message: "first deploy" });
let current = release;
while (!["active", "sleeping", "failed", "canceled", "stopped", "removed"].includes(current.state)) {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 3000));
  current = await miosa.services.release(service.id, release.id);
}
console.log(current.state);
```

The Python SDK ships `wait_for_release(service_id, release_id)`, which polls and raises on a failed release.

A release goes `queued -> building -> built -> starting -> health_check -> active`.
Any step can fail; the release carries a `reason.code` such as `build_failed`, `healthcheck_timeout` or `no_capacity`.

## 3. Add Postgres and Redis

Templates create the service, its variables and the references between them in one change set:

```bash
miosa service templates                       # the catalog
miosa service templates apply shop nextjs-postgres
miosa service templates apply shop redis
```

The Postgres template creates a database service and a web service whose `DATABASE_URL` is the reference `${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}`.
Applying a template stages one change set and deploys every service it creates; pass `--no-deploy` to create them without deploying.

To read the connection string later:

```bash
miosa service connection shop Postgres
```

That call needs `databases:read` and is audited, because the URL holds the password.

## 4. Add a worker

A worker has no port and no address.

```bash
miosa service create shop Worker --type worker \
  --repo https://github.com/acme/api \
  --start-command "node worker.js" \
  --replicas 1
miosa service deploy shop Worker
```

The worker can read the same database with the same reference:

```bash
miosa service vars set shop Worker DATABASE_URL='${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}'
```

## 5. Attach a domain

A web service or static site gets a public address on `miosa.app`:

```bash
miosa service domains shop API
miosa service domains enable shop API --label api
```

The result is `https://api.<your-org>.miosa.app`, served from the active release's healthy replicas.
To stop serving publicly without deleting the service, remove the address:

```bash
miosa service domains disable shop API
```

Private networking between services is not available yet, so other services call it at its public address; databases are reached through their connection variables, see [addresses and domains](/docs/services/domains).

## 6. Read a failed release

```bash
miosa service releases shop API
miosa service logs shop API
```

`logs` prints the newest release's state transitions and its failure reason.
Pass `--release <number>` to look at an older one.
The console's Logs tab shows each replica's runtime lines and the build log; see [Logs](/docs/services/logs).

## 7. Roll back

Rollback serves an earlier release's built image with its frozen source and settings.
Nothing is rebuilt, so it is fast.

```bash
miosa service rollback shop API 3 --yes
```

`miosa service promote shop API 3` is the same call: the Services API calls the operation rollback.

## 8. Tear down

```bash
miosa service stop shop API --yes      # stop now, keep the service
miosa service delete shop API --yes    # remove it and stop its replicas
```

Deleting a database service also deletes its data, so it takes `--confirm <exact name>` instead of `--yes`.
See [Deleting a database service](/docs/services/cli#deleting-a-database-service).

services/releases:
A release is one build-and-serve attempt of a service.
It is immutable: it freezes the source, the settings and the built image it ran with.

## Deploy

```bash
miosa service deploy shop API                        # rebuild the service's own source
miosa service deploy shop API --dir . --wait         # upload a directory
miosa service deploy shop API --repo https://github.com/acme/api --branch main
miosa service deploy shop API --image ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4 --port 8080
```

Every release takes an `Idempotency-Key`; the CLI sends one so a retried command returns the first release instead of starting a second.

`--wait` follows the release and exits non-zero if it fails, printing the reason.

## The state machine

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `queued` | Accepted, waiting for a worker. |
| `building` | The source is being built. |
| `built` | The image exists; the release is about to start replicas. |
| `pre_deploy` | `pre_deploy_command` is running in the new replica. |
| `starting` | Replicas are booting. |
| `health_check` | The health path is being probed. |
| `active` | Serving. |
| `sleeping` | Idle sleep stopped the replicas; the next request wakes them. |
| `draining` | An earlier release is stopping. |
| `crashed` | A replica crashed and the restart policy did not recover it. |
| `failed` | Terminal failure, with a reason. |
| `canceled` | Canceled by a user. |
| `stopped` | Stopped by `stop`. |

A release that never leaves a state before its deadline is settled by the reaper with `deadline_exceeded`.

## Read a failure

```bash
miosa service releases shop API
miosa service logs shop API
miosa service logs shop API --release 6
```

`logs` prints every transition and the failure reason of the newest release, or of the release you name.
The release events carry the reason a release failed.
The build log and each replica's runtime lines are in the console's Logs tab; see [Logs](/docs/services/logs). The CLI does not stream them.

What a running replica printed is a separate read:

```text
GET /projects/:id/services/:sid/logs                    # the active release
GET /projects/:id/services/:sid/deployments/:did/logs   # one release
```

Each returns the last lines of every replica's output, with your secret values masked.
`tail` sets the number of lines (1 to 1000, default 200) and `replica` narrows it to one replica.
A replica that cannot be read says so in its own entry and does not hide the others.
It is a snapshot, not a stream.

Common reason codes:

| Code | What to do |
|---|---|
| `build_failed` | Read the build output; the command exited non-zero. |
| `clone_failed` | The repository or branch was not reachable, or the credential is wrong. |
| `image_pull_failed` | The image reference is wrong, or the registry secret is missing. |
| `healthcheck_timeout` | The app did not answer its health path in time. Check `start_command` and the port. |
| `pre_deploy_failed` | `pre_deploy_command` exited non-zero; nothing serves. |
| `no_capacity` | No host had room for the shape in that region. Try another region or a smaller `limits`. |
| `reference_missing` | A variable references something that does not exist. `miosa service vars effective` lists them. |
| `reference_cycle` | Two variables reference each other. |
| `deadline_exceeded` | The release sat in one state too long and the reaper settled it. |
| `quota_exceeded` | A plan limit was reached. |

## Promote and roll back

Rollback serves an earlier release's built image with its frozen source and settings.
Nothing is rebuilt, so it is fast.

```bash
miosa service rollback shop API 3 --yes
miosa service promote  shop API 3 --yes   # the same call
```

The Services API has one operation for this and calls it rollback.
The CLI accepts `promote` as its name for "serve this release again"; there is no separate promote route.

## Cancel and remove

```bash
miosa service cancel shop API 7     # a queued or building release
miosa service release shop API 3    # one release
```

A release that already finished can be removed from the history; one that is still running cannot.

## Stop, start, restart

```bash
miosa service stop    shop API --yes   # stop every active release now
miosa service start   shop API         # start a stopped service
miosa service restart shop API         # queue a release that restarts it
```

`stop` fails with `SERVICES_NOT_STOPPED` if a replica cannot be stopped, so a service is never reported stopped while it still runs.
`start` on a service that is already running or starting is `SERVICE_CONFLICT`.

## Rollout and rollback of several services

Each service releases independently.
For a coordinated change, apply a template or a change set, which stages every service's change and deploys them together.
services/replicas:
A replica is one running copy of a service.
A service runs from 1 to 50 replicas.

## Change replicas, region and size

```bash
miosa service update shop API --replicas 4
miosa service scale  shop API --replicas 4
```

`update` changes the setting.
`scale` changes replicas, region or limits and also queues a release that applies them.
The running release is not touched until that release is active, so a scale change never interrupts traffic part way.

| Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `replicas` | 1 to 50. A writable volume forces 1. |
| `region` | `us-west`, `us-east` or `us-mia`. |
| `limits` | `{vcpu, memory_mb}`. Above 4 vCPU or 8192 MB the release fails. |
| `restart_policy` | `always`, `on_failure` or `never`. |
| `healthcheck_path` | The path a web service must answer before a new release becomes active. |

## What a release does to replicas

A new release starts its replicas first.
Once they pass the health check, the release becomes `active` and the earlier release drains and stops.
`overlap_s` and `terminate_grace_s` add time before the earlier release stops.

## Volumes

A volume is attached to a service, never added on its own.
A writable volume allows one replica.
Mount it read-only if you need more.
A service can mount up to four volumes, and a path or a volume cannot repeat.

## Check what takes effect

```bash
miosa service settings shop
```

Each setting is `enforced`, `stored` or `unsupported`.
A `stored` setting is kept but not applied yet, so do not rely on it.

## Examples

TypeScript:

```typescript
import { Miosa } from "@miosa/sdk";

const miosa = new Miosa({ apiKey: process.env.MIOSA_API_KEY! });

const project = await miosa.projects.create({
  name: "Shop",
  workspaceId: process.env.MIOSA_WORKSPACE_ID!,
});

const api = await miosa.services.create(project.id, {
  name: "API",
  type: "web",
  source: { type: "git", ref: "https://github.com/acme/api" },
  settings: { start_command: "node server.js", replicas: 2 },
});

await miosa.services.enablePublicAddress(api.id);
const release = await miosa.services.deploy(api.id, { message: "first deploy" });
console.log(release.number, release.state);
```

Python:

```python
from miosa import Miosa

miosa = Miosa(api_key=os.environ["MIOSA_API_KEY"])

project = miosa.projects.create("Shop", workspace_id=os.environ["MIOSA_WORKSPACE_ID"])

```

## Async

The Python SDK has the same surface under `AsyncMiosa`, with `await` on every method and an async `wait_for_release`.
services/services:
A service's `kind` is what the API stores.
It is one of `server`, `worker`, `cron`, `static` or `database`.
The product types map onto it:

| Product type | `kind` | Public address |
|---|---|---|
| Web service | `server` | Yes, when enabled |
| Private service | `server` | No |
| Worker | `worker` | No |
| Static site | `static` | Yes, when enabled |
| Cron job | `cron` | No |
| Database service | `database` | No (use `connection`) |

There is no `web` or `private` kind.
The CLI and both SDKs take `type: web` or `type: private`, and store `kind: server`.
A private service is a server service with no public address.

## Source

A service builds from one source.

| `source.type` | What it needs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `git` | `ref` (repository URL), optional `branch` and `root_dir` | Built on a Services build cell |
| `image` | `ref` (OCI image), optional `port`, optional `registry_secret` | The image is run as-is |
| `upload` | `upload_id` | PUT a `.tar.gz`, `.tar.zst`, `.tar` or `.zip` archive first |
| `forge` | `ref` | A repository hosted by MIOSA Forge |

Dockerfile builds run on the Services build cells and are detected in the source.
While the build cells are off, a Dockerfile service does not build; use a git build or an image source.

Uploading a directory is one command:

```bash
miosa service deploy shop API --dir . --wait
```

The CLI packs the directory (skipping `.git`, `node_modules` and `.env*`), records the archive with `POST /uploads`, PUTs it to the returned URL and deploys `{source: {type: "upload", upload_id}}`.
Archives are single use and expire after an hour.

## Settings

Settings are validated strictly: an unknown key is refused, so a typo never silently stays.

| Setting | Applies to | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `start_command` | all | Replaces the image entrypoint when a replica starts. |
| `pre_deploy_command` | all | Runs once in the new replica before the app starts. A non-zero exit fails the release. |
| `healthcheck_path` | `server` | The path probed before a new release becomes active. |
| `healthcheck_timeout_s` | `server` | How long a release may take to pass. |
| `restart_policy` | all | `always`, `on_failure` or `never`. |
| `max_retries` | all | Restarts before an `on_failure` replica is left stopped. |
| `replicas` | all | 1 to 50. A writable volume forces 1. |
| `region` | all | `us-west`, `us-east` or `us-mia`. |
| `limits` | all | `{vcpu, memory_mb}`. Above 4 vCPU or 8192 MB the release fails. |
| `sleep` | services with a public address | `{enabled, idle_s}`. The next request wakes the service. |
| `cron_schedule` | `cron` | Required. Five-field cron, UTC. |
| `overlap_s` | all | Extra time before the previous release is stopped. |
| `terminate_grace_s` | all | Extra time before the previous release is stopped, like `overlap_s`. |
| `volumes` | `server`, `worker` | Up to four `{volume, mount_path, read_only}`. |

Read what each setting actually does on your platform:

```bash
miosa service settings shop
```

Each entry is `enforced` (it takes effect), `stored` (kept but not applied yet) or `unsupported`.
Never present a `stored` setting as if it took effect.

## Create and change

```bash
miosa service create shop API --type web --repo https://github.com/acme/api --replicas 2
miosa service update shop API --replicas 4
miosa service scale  shop API --replicas 4        # also queues a release
```

`update` merges settings: only the flags you pass change.
It sends the `lock_version` it read; a stale value is refused with `STALE_SERVICE` so two editors cannot overwrite each other.
`scale` changes replicas, region or limits and queues a release that applies them.

## Cron jobs

```bash
miosa service create shop Nightly --type schedule \
  --repo https://github.com/acme/api \
  --start-command "node jobs/nightly.js" \
  --schedule "0 3 * * *"
miosa service runs shop Nightly --output
```

`runs` shows the newest 20 runs with state, exit code, times and output.
A run is limited to five minutes.

## Database services

A database service is a managed Postgres or Redis bound to the project.
Apply a template to create one with its variables wired, or attach an existing managed database.
The connection string is only available through `connection`, which is audited:

```bash
miosa service connection shop Postgres
```

## Limits and errors

| Error | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND` | No service with that id in the project. The API resolves services by id only. |
| `STALE_SERVICE` | The `lock_version` you sent is older than the stored one. Re-read and retry. |
| `SERVICE_CONFLICT` | `start` on a service that is already running or starting. |
| `SERVICES_NOT_STOPPED` | `stop` could not stop a replica; the service stays running. |
| `INGRESS_DISABLED` | Public addresses are off for this platform; the service runs but has no address to reach it on. |
| `PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED` | The plan's service limit is reached. |
services/static:
A static service takes a git source like a web service does, and is served from
the static lane instead of a container.

```bash
miosa service create shop site --type static \
  --repo https://github.com/acme/site --branch main
miosa service update shop site --build-command "npm run build" --output-dir dist
```

## How the site is built

The build runs on a build cell: Railpack detects the framework, or a Dockerfile
in the repository is used when there is one. `build_command` replaces the build
command Railpack would use (Railpack builds only), and `output_dir` says which
folder to serve.

With neither set, the output folder is discovered: Railpack's own static root
first, then `dist`, `build`, `out`, `public` and `_site`, taking the first one
with an `index.html` at its top. A Dockerfile build also tries the image's own
document root (`nginx`, `httpd`, `caddy`).

## When the build fails

- `reason_code: build_failed` with `reason_detail` starting
  `static_output_missing:` means no `index.html` was found in any candidate
  folder. Set `output_dir` to the folder your build writes.
- `static_site_too_large:` means the site is over 500 MiB or over 20,000 files.

> **Note: Framework example**
>
> A Vite site needs nothing: Railpack detects Vite, builds it, and the output is
> `dist`. Single-page-app fallback routing is a separate change; until then a deep
> link into a client-side route should be handled by the app.
services/variables:
Variables are stored sealed at rest.
A read returns a masked preview, never the value.
The only plaintext read is `reveal`, which needs `env:reveal` and a person's own credential, and which refuses a sealed variable.

## Set a variable

```bash
miosa service vars set shop API NODE_ENV=production
miosa service vars list shop API
```

TypeScript:

```typescript
await miosa.services.setVariables(serviceId, { NODE_ENV: "production" });
const variables = await miosa.services.variables(serviceId);
```

Python:

```python
miosa.services.set_variables(service_id, {"NODE_ENV": "production"})
variables = miosa.services.variables(service_id)
```

A write merges by name. Deleting takes names:

```bash
miosa service vars unset shop API NODE_ENV,OLD_FLAG
```

## References

A value may be a reference.
MIOSA resolves it when the release starts, so the service always sees the current value.

| Expression | Resolves to |
|---|---|
| `${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}` | A variable of another service in the same environment |
| `${{shared.API_BASE}}` | An environment shared variable |
| `${{NAME}}` | Another variable of the same service |
| `${{secret(32)}}` | A generated random secret of 32 characters |

```bash
miosa service vars set shop API DATABASE_URL='${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}'
```

Quote the value in a shell so `${{...}}` reaches MIOSA unchanged.

A cycle or a malformed expression is refused with every problem at once, and nothing is written.
A reference to a service or variable that does not exist yet is allowed to be saved, but it blocks the deploy and shows up under `problems`.

## Shared variables

Shared variables belong to the environment and are visible to every service in it.

```bash
miosa project vars set shop API_BASE=https://api.acme.dev
miosa project vars list shop
miosa project vars unset shop API_BASE
```

A service reads one with `${{shared.API_BASE}}`.

## When a change needs a release

Writing a variable does not change the running release.
MIOSA records what the write made stale on the service document as `pending_changes`:

```json
{"needs": "rebuild", "variables": ["DATABASE_URL"], "because": "Web.DATABASE_URL", "at": "..."}
```

- `needs: rebuild` when a build-visible variable changed, because a redeploy alone would ship the value inlined at build time.
- `needs: redeploy` for every other variable, which is read when the release starts.
- `because` is `own`, `shared`, or the reference that carried the change: changing `Web.DATABASE_URL` marks every service whose expression uses it, and changing a shared variable marks every service that reads it.

```bash
miosa service get shop API
```

A deploy clears the mark, and a rebuild is never downgraded by a later runtime change:

```bash
miosa service deploy shop API
```

## Check what a deploy will receive

```bash
miosa service vars effective shop API
```

This shows every variable the release will receive, with references resolved and values still masked, plus a `problems` list.
A release is refused while that list is not empty.

## Read one value

```bash
miosa service vars reveal shop API DATABASE_URL
```

Reveal is for a person acting as themselves.
A sealed variable never reveals, and every reveal is audited with the variable's name and never its value.

## Build-time variables

A variable can be marked build-visible, so the build sees it too.
Platform-provided values are never sent to a build.
Names starting with `MIOSA_` or `RAILPACK_` are reserved.
